public_rationale: The conditional forecast cannot yet be scored. The record does not establish that its antecedent occurred, and the spending threshold has several material ambiguities. Microsoft's September-quarter figure alone does not settle the condition. The absence of a documented collapse does not make an undated conditional forecast false.
limitations: No comprehensive, comparable spending series was verified for all named hyperscalers through the cutoff.
The outcome and timing thresholds require interpretation.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If hyperscalers cut capex significantly (below $15 billion), the AI bubble will pop.
conditions: hyperscalers drop capex significantly, below $15 billion

statement.excerpt: Yet the moment they stop spending capex (by which I mean dropping it significantly — below $15 billion, I’d say), the AI bubble pops.
statement.document_title: The More You Buy, The More You Lose

our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion identifies Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet and Meta as the hyperscalers.
The references to their last quarters suggest quarterly spending, but the statement does not specify whether $15 billion applies individually or collectively.
I read 'bubble pops' as a broad, substantial collapse in AI-linked valuations and financing, rather than an isolated stock decline.
The forecast has no deadline. 'The moment' requires a close temporal connection after the spending reduction, but supplies no precise response window.
criteria.support_condition: A verified post-publication reduction below the specified spending threshold, followed promptly by a broad collapse in AI-linked valuations and financing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A verified qualifying reduction followed by sustained AI valuations and financing through a defensible interpretation of the immediate response window. Without an established antecedent, the forecast cannot be scored.
